image_description: An underwater photograph showing a hammerhead shark swimming over a sandy seabed. The shark is viewed from a high-angle, rear-three-quarter perspective, displaying its distinctive T-shaped head, dorsal fin, pectoral fins, and caudal fin. The water is slightly murky with a greenish-blue tint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic T-shaped, laterally expanded head structure characteristic of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots corresponding to eyes are visible at the very ends of the horizontal head extensions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Due to the viewing angle (from above/behind) and image resolution, the nostrils on the ventral side or precise lateral margin are not distinctly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the head appears straight/slightly curved, consistent with the taxonomy description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape tapers smoothly towards the tail and appears thin from this angle, indicating lateral compression.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is dark grey/brown. While the ventral side is mostly hidden, the visible lower edges suggest lighter coloration, consistent with countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution and water turbidity prevent microscopic verification of dermal denticles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, tall, triangular/falcate dorsal fin is clearly visible in the correct anterior position relative to the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are visible extending from the body, appearing broad and roughly triangular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin shows the classic shark heterocercal structure with a larger upper lobe.
